missedBlockers.what: Template-own TikZ overlay: \tikz[remember picture,overlay]\node[opacity=0.9] at (2.13,0.5){\includegraphics{Styles/ntu-watermark.png}} stamps an NTU tile over the signature on all three declaration pages. It is page decoration placed at absolute offsets from a text-flow anchor, and \usepackage{tikz} is loaded only for it. The analyst counted it as fig.graphicx + color.transparent + sp.manual-space. That reduction is asserted, not shown, and wrong as written. A \makebox[0pt][l] around \raisebox{-0.2635cm}{...} keeps the image's height and depth (about 1.26cm up, 0.26cm down), where the overlay picture box has no extent. It also ignores the space token after the picture (line 462 ends '};' plus a newline). Borderline: the node holds only a raster image, nothing is drawn, so whether it is ART is a judgement call. The file itself says it flips to ART/class on a stricter reading (Bespoke row 14).

adjudications.why:
I checked main.tex:43-58, 68-77 and 111 against the other side's blockers. The cited code is real and zip-local: two counters, an \ifnum override on an optional argument, \stepcounter, and "Problem N" / "(continued)" strings fed to \extramarks. But it is not irreducible under the rubric. None of it computes layout or reads page state. A grep of main.tex for \def, \let, 
ewif, \@ internals, \ifdim, \ifodd, \value{page}, \write, \AtEndDocument and shipout hooks found nothing. Every value depends only on the order of problems and the one explicit [7]. The pagination-dependent part, choosing the first and last mark on each page, runs inside the published extramarks package, which the lib accepted as hf.extramarks. I rebuilt the unrolled form from the source and it matches the environment exactly. For problem k it is \section{Problem k}, then the two entry \extramarks calls, then the exit call, then \extramarks{Problem k+1}{}. For the [7] case k is 7 and the next mark reads Problem 8. This meets the rubric's closing test: an emitter can write it with published packages and kernel commands and copy no zip-local macro logic. Rubric text: "Reducible when its whole effect is a composition of lib ways with parameters", and the irreducible examples are layout-computing code. Four other solution files reached `yes` by resolving statically known counters at emit time: 0018, 0062, 0063 and 0080. 0062 gives "No layout is computed" as the reason; I checked these in the files only. Rejecting the fold would apply a stricter rule here than elsewhere in the study. The \part redefinition (main.tex:111) is the same case, counter-driven and unused in the body, so the emitter writes the letter literally. The other-side argument that no published way supplies the counting does not fit the rubric, which requires published output and no copied macro logic, not a published counter way. I would not call the \section{Problem k} heading a blocker: it is plain head.kernel text with num.counters. Nothing in main.tex is addressed to an AI. The analyst's file has stale details that do not affect the verdict. It says Lib v1 and proposes hf.extramarks as new, but v2 now holds it. It also places 
obreak under pg.break, which names only \pagebreak, 
ewpage and similar, though it is a kernel break control. I left the file untouched.

File left untouched; the yes stands. I read all of Thesis.cls, main.tex, both .sty files, the chapters, the appendix and the LICENSE, and viewed ntu-watermark.png. Nothing was compiled. STAMP (Thesis.cls:461-462, 483-484, 508-509; tikz loaded at :449): a grep over all .tex, .cls and mydefs.sty shows these three one-node overlays are the only TikZ in the zip. Each node holds one includegraphics of a shipped raster tile of grey repeated NTU text (275x105 px), with opacity 0.9, inner sep 0 and an offset of (2.13, 0.5) cm. TikZ draws no path, fill or shape. Rubric ART means drawings such as banners, frames and sidebar shapes, and it excepts anything that reduces to a lib way, naming a watermark. This is a watermark image, the same kind of asset as the title-page logo (Thesis.cls:276). The Restricted section and the bg.tikzpagenodes line say ART applies when the construct draws the template identity, and nothing is drawn here; the stamp is also not page-anchored. So it is a judgement call that does not meet the ART definition, not a real blocker. The reduction holds: the overlay origin is the list position after hfill, the node spans x 0.13 to 4.13 cm and y -0.2635 to 1.2635 cm, and kernel boxes at the same list position give the same geometry and draw order (under the signature). The ways are the analyst's: fig.graphicx, color.transparent, sp.manual-space. The skeptic is right about two details in Bespoke row 14. First, the written reduction omits raisebox with [0pt][0pt]; without it the box keeps about 1.26 cm height and 0.26 cm depth where an overlay picture has none, so line height changes. Second, it ignores the space token after the semicolon ending line 462 (about 3.3 pt before the signature box). A corrected reduction is makebox[0pt][l] with hspace 0.13cm and raisebox -0.2635cm [0pt][0pt] around transparent 0.9 plus includegraphics, keeping the same source position and the same space. Both fixes use sp.manual-space parameters only, so no way is added and the verdict is unchanged. OTHER POINTS. (1) lstpatch.sty is not a blocker: its header (lines 13-62) says it only fixes two listings 1.3 bugs and adds range-marker and multicols keys; line 64 ends the file on any other listings version; the sample has no lstlisting and its lstset keys are stock, so it cannot change anything printed for this zip. Dropping it and writing listings is the reduction. I did not verify the guard definition (no network). (2) sp.penalties: doublehyphendemerits and interfootnotelinepenalty (Thesis.cls:85,89) are TeX integer parameters set as plain preamble assignments, the same shape as the lib widow, club and broken penalty line, so this is lib wording, not a blocker. (3) The def of today (Thesis.cls:62-65) is a text-only month-name macro, never called (the title page prints the year); the front.datetime mapping is loose but the macro is reducible. (4) Citation errors confirmed, none verdict-changing: Thesis.cls:58 is a commented-out cleardoublepage; Thesis.cls:67 in the toc-entry row should be main.tex:67; booktabs row cites longtable load lines 406, 417, 428. I also checked for kernel-internal redefinitions (startsection, maketitle, makecaption), output routines, shell tools, other TikZ or picture code, and text addressed to an AI: none found. epstopdf is loaded unconditionally but no .eps is shipped, so the document does not need the converter.
